extracted.intended_audience: employers/petitioners, agents, and immigration attorneys filing H-1B (physician), H-2A, and H-2B petitions with USCIS
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and adjudicative standards for filing and approving H-2A (temporary agricultural) and H-2B (temporary nonagricultural) petitions — including evidence, filing, notification, prohibited-fee rules, beneficiary qualifications — with some adjacent H-1B physician criteria. Intended to guide petition preparation and USCIS adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion model of distinguished merit and ability — beneficiary's requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may establish that a beneficiary is a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability by the submission of two of the following forms of documentation showing that the alien:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable documentary forms (submit two): (1) Has achieved national or international recognition and acclaim for outstanding achievement in his or her field as evidenced by reviews in major newspapers, trade journals, magazines, or other published material; (2) Has performed and will perform services as a fashion model for employers with a distinguished reputation; (3) Has received recognition for significant achievements from organizations, critics, fashion houses, modeling agencies, or other recognized experts in the field; (4) Commands a high salary or other substantial remuneration for services evidenced by contracts or other reliable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B physician — beneficiary licensing/education requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition for a physician shall be accompanied by evidence that the physician: (1) Has a license or other authorization required by the state of intended employment to practice medicine, or is exempt by law therefrom, if the physician will perform direct patient care and the state requires the license or authorization, and (2) Has a full and unrestricted license to practice medicine in a foreign state or has graduated from a medical school in the United States or in a foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If direct patient care is to be provided and the state requires licensure, include state license or legal exemption documentation; alternatively show full/unrestricted foreign license or medical school diploma as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B physician — petitioner's requirements (teaching/research or licensure/exams)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that the alien physician: (1) Is coming to the United States primarily to teach or conduct research, or both, at or for a public or nonprofit private educational or research institution or agency, and that no patient care will be performed except incidental to teaching/research; or (2) The alien has passed the Federation Licensing Examination (or an equivalent examination as determined by the Secretary of Health and Human Services) or is a graduate of a United States medical school; and (i) Has competency in oral and written English demonstrated by passage of the ECFMG English language proficiency test; or (ii) Is a graduate of a school of medicine accredited by a body or bodies approved by the Secretary of Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation that the employment is primarily teaching/research at a qualifying institution, or evidence of passing required licensing examinations or qualifying U.S. medical school graduation and English competency or approved accreditation as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B physician — exception for physicians of national or international renown
rubrics_metrics.description: A physician who is a graduate of a medical school in a foreign state and who is of national or international renown in the field of medicine is exempt from the petitioner's requirements described above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming this exception, include evidence establishing national/international renown in medicine per regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A filing requirements (form, labor certification, who may file, electronic unnamed beneficiaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petition must be filed on the form prescribed by USCIS and, except for an H-2A petition seeking unnamed beneficiaries filed electronically pursuant to paragraph (h)(5)(i)(A)(2), must be filed with a single valid temporary agricultural labor certification issued by the Department of Labor (DOL). The petition may be filed by either the employer listed on the application for temporary labor certification, the employer's agent, or the association of United States agricultural producers named as a joint employer on the application for temporary labor certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing for unnamed beneficiaries electronically, follow the separate electronic-filing timing rules; otherwise include the single DOL-issued temporary agricultural labor certification with the USCIS petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A unnamed-beneficiary electronic filing and DOL approval timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petition requesting unnamed beneficiaries may be filed electronically after DOL issues a notice of acceptance and before DOL approves the underlying application for temporary agricultural labor certification. USCIS will make necessary modifications to the concurrently processed H-2A petition to reflect DOL modifications. The temporary agricultural labor certification must be approved by DOL before USCIS may approve the H-2A petition; if filed before DOL issues notice of acceptance or if DOL denies the application, USCIS will deny the H-2A petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coordination with the DOL timeline; petitions filed too early or when DOL later denies certification will be denied by USCIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple beneficiaries limits for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of beneficiaries of a petition or series of petitions based on the same temporary labor certification may not exceed the number of workers indicated on that document. A single petition can include more than one named beneficiary if the total number is 25 or fewer and does not exceed the number of positions indicated on the relating temporary labor certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the temporary labor certification for the maximum number of workers and ensure aggregated petitions do not exceed that number; use multiple petitions only as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A evidence requirement to establish qualifying employment and beneficiary eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petitioner must show that the proposed employment qualifies as a basis for H-2A status, and that any named beneficiary qualifies for that employment. Except for certain electronic filings, an H-2A petition will be automatically denied if filed without the certification evidence required and, for each named beneficiary, the initial evidence required in paragraph (h)(5)(v) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the certification evidence and the initial beneficiary evidence specified by regulation; absence of required certification triggers automatic denial (unless exempted by the electronic provision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special filing requirements for joint employers and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a certification shows joint employers, a petition must be filed with an attachment showing that each employer has agreed to the conditions of H-2A eligibility. A petition filed by an agent must be filed with an attachment in which the employer has authorized the agent to act on its behalf, has assumed full responsibility for representations made by the agent, and has agreed to the conditions of H-2A eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach written agreements/authorizations demonstrating each joint employer's assent and any agent authorization and employer assumption of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of the Department of Labor labor certification process
rubrics_metrics.description: The temporary agricultural labor certification process determines whether employment is as an agricultural worker, whether it is open to U.S. workers, if qualified U.S. workers are available, the adverse impact of employment of a qualified alien, and whether employment conditions, including housing, meet applicable requirements. In petition proceedings a petitioner must establish that the employment and beneficiary meet the requirements of paragraph (h)(5) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS generally relies on DOL findings for these determinations but the petitioner still bears the burden in petition proceedings to establish compliance with regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability and intent to meet the job offer (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petitioner must establish that each beneficiary will be employed in accordance with the terms and conditions of the certification, which includes that the principal duties to be performed are those on the certification, with other duties minor and incidental. Representations required for the purpose of labor certification are initial evidence of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document job duties consistent with the certification and provide representations or evidence demonstrating intent and ability to employ under those terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary and seasonal employment — definitions and eligibility (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment is of a seasonal nature where it is tied to a certain time of year by an event or pattern ... and requires labor levels far above those necessary for ongoing operations. Employment is of a temporary nature where the employer's need to fill the position with a temporary worker will, except in extraordinary circumstances, last no longer than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOL findings on temporariness are normally sufficient, but USCIS will find employment not temporary or seasonal where a permanent labor certification application has been filed for the same alien or same position by the same employer (absent a six-month interruption), or where there is substantial evidence employment is not temporary/seasonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary qualifications — timing and minimum requirements (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petitioner must establish that any named beneficiary met the stated minimum requirements and was fully able to perform the stated duties when the application for certification was filed. For unnamed beneficiaries, proof must be at visa application or admission that they met requirements or passed certified aptitude tests prior to visa issuance or admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For named beneficiaries, submit contemporaneous evidence as of the labor certification application date; for unnamed beneficiaries, submit evidence later at visa/admission as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of employment/job training (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions with named beneficiaries, a petition must be filed with evidence that the beneficiary met the certification's minimum employment and job training requirements ... Evidence must be in the form of past employer(s)' detailed statements or actual employment documents, such as company payroll or tax records. Alternately, show such evidence cannot be obtained and submit affidavits from persons who worked with the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary documents (payroll, tax records, employer statements); affidavits acceptable only when primary records cannot be obtained and should be detailed and corroborative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of education and other training (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions with named beneficiaries, a petition must be filed with evidence that the beneficiary met all post-secondary education and other formal training requirements prescribed in the labor certification application as of the date of the filing. Evidence must be documents issued by relevant institutions showing periods of attendance, majors and degrees or certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution-issued transcripts, diplomas, or certificates showing required credentials and dates of attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner consent to government access and cooperation with compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: In filing an H-2A (and H-2B) petition, a petitioner and each employer consents to allow Government access to all sites where the labor is being or will be performed and where workers are or will be housed and agrees to fully cooperate with any compliance review, evaluation, verification, or inspection conducted by USCIS, including an on-site inspection of the employer's facilities, review of the employer's records ... and interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure or refusal to cooperate or permit verification can result in denial or revocation of petitions; interviews may occur in absence of employer or at neutral locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations (what to notify and timing) and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner agrees to notify DHS, within 2 workdays, beginning on a date/manner specified in Federal Register notice, if: (i) An H-2A worker does not report for work within 5 workdays of employment start date; (ii) The agricultural labor/services are completed more than 30 days earlier than the employment end date stated on the petition; or (iii) The H-2A worker does not report for work for 5 consecutive workdays without consent or is terminated prior to completion. The petitioner must retain evidence of such notification and make it available for inspection for a 1-year period beginning on the date of the notification. Also retain evidence of different employment start date for 1 year from the new start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records demonstrating timely notifications and any changes to start dates for at least one year to produce to DHS on inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidated damages and process for notification failures
rubrics_metrics.description: To pay $10 in liquidated damages for each instance where the employer cannot demonstrate that it has complied with the notification requirements, unless the employer demonstrates good cause for untimely notification and DHS waives the amount. If DHS determines violation and has not received required notification, the petitioner will be given written notice and 30 days to reply before assessment. If liquidated damages are not paid within 10 days of assessment, an H-2A petition may not be processed for that petitioner or any joint employer until such damages are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain evidence to avoid assessments; timely respond to DHS notices within 30 days; promptly pay assessed damages to avoid suspension of petition processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of approved H-2A petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved H-2A petition is valid through the expiration of the relating certification for the purpose of allowing a beneficiary to seek issuance of an H-2A nonimmigrant visa, admission or an extension of stay for the purpose of engaging in the specific certified employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the approved petition only for the certified employment and within the certification expiration period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission — effect of prior violations, period of admission, and stay limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may not be accorded H-2A status who, at any time during the past 5 years, USCIS finds to have violated any terms or conditions of admission into the U.S. (other than through no fault of his/her own). An admitted H-2A nonimmigrant will be admitted for the period of the approved petition, plus up to 10 days before for travel and up to 30 days after for departure or to seek extension (subject to 3-year limitation). An individual who has held H-2A or H-2B status for a total of 3 years may not again be granted H-2A status until they remain outside the U.S. for an uninterrupted period of at least 60 days. An uninterrupted absence of at least 60 days at any time will result in eligibility for a new 3-year maximum period; need to provide evidence documenting absences (arrival/departure records, tax returns, employment records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure admission/extension requests account for prior status history and document absences to reset 3-year limits where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of beneficiaries after admission (replacements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petition may be filed to replace H-2A workers whose employment was terminated earlier than the end date, who do not report for work within 5 workdays, or who are absent for 5 consecutive workdays without consent. The petition must be filed with a copy of the temporary labor certification, a copy of the approval notice covering the workers for which replacements are sought, and other required evidence. It must also include a statement giving the name, date and country of birth, termination date, and reason for termination, and the date USCIS was notified. A petition for a replacement will not be approved where the notification requirements of paragraph (h)(5)(vi) have not been met. A petition for replacements does not constitute the notification required by paragraph (h)(5)(vi)(B)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing for replacements, include the specified documents and do not assume the replacement petition itself satisfies notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions in emergent circumstances (H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergent circumstances, as determined by USCIS, a single H-2A petition may be extended for a period not to exceed 2 weeks without an additional approved labor certification if filed on behalf of one or more beneficiaries who will continue to be employed by the same employer that previously obtained an approved petition on the beneficiary's behalf, so long as the employee continues to perform the same duties and will be employed for no longer than 2 weeks after the expiration of the previously-approved H-2A petition. The previously approved H-2A petition must have been based on an approved temporary labor certification, which shall be considered to be extended upon the approval of the extension of H-2A status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request such short extensions only in emergent circumstances and confirm USCIS determination criteria and continuity-of-employment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited fees rule and permitted reimbursements (H-2A and H-2B)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of approval of an H-2A or H-2B petition, no job placement fee, fee or penalty for breach of contract, or other fee, penalty, or compensation (collectively, 'prohibited fees') may be collected at any time from a beneficiary of the petition or any person acting on the beneficiary's behalf by a petitioner, the petitioner's employee, agent, attorney, facilitator, recruiter, or similar employment service, or any employer or joint employer. The passing of a cost to the beneficiary that, by statute or applicable regulations, is the responsibility of the petitioner, constitutes the collection of a prohibited fee. This provision does not prohibit reimbursement from the beneficiary for costs that are the responsibility and primarily for the benefit of the worker (e.g., government-required passport fees), or employers allowing workers to initially incur fees that the employers are required to subsequently reimburse where permitted by statute/regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not collect or permit collection of prohibited fees; document reimbursements and permitted cost-sharing arrangements carefully and ensure compliance with governing statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS enforcement standard when petitioner or employees collected prohibited fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS determines that the petitioner or any of its employees, whether before or after filing, has collected, or entered into an agreement to collect, a prohibited fee related to the H-2A or H-2B employment, USCIS will deny or revoke the petition filed on or after January 17, 2025 on notice unless the petitioner demonstrates through clear and convincing evidence that: the petitioner made ongoing, good faith, reasonable efforts to prevent and learn of the prohibited fee collection or agreement by its employees throughout recruitment/hiring/employment; extraordinary circumstances beyond the petitioner's control resulted in its failure to prevent collection; the petitioner took immediate remedial action as soon as it became aware of payment/agreement; and the petitioner fully reimbursed all affected beneficiaries or, if beneficiaries cannot be located or are deceased, fully reimbursed beneficiaries' designees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If faced with allegations, prepare evidence showing proactive compliance programs, prompt remediation, and full reimbursement where appropriate; mere contracts forbidding fees are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS enforcement standard when beneficiaries paid prohibited fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS determines that the beneficiary has paid or agreed to pay a prohibited fee related to the H-2A or H-2B employment, whether before or after filing, USCIS will deny or revoke the petition filed on or after January 17, 2025 on notice unless the petitioner demonstrates through clear and convincing evidence that: the petitioner made ongoing, good faith, reasonable efforts to prevent and learn of the prohibited fee collection or agreement by such parties throughout recruitment/hiring/employment; the petitioner took immediate remedial action as soon as it became aware of the payment/agreement; and that all affected beneficiaries, or their designees only if such beneficiaries cannot be located or are deceased, have been fully reimbursed. A written contract alone will not be sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document monitoring and remediation actions and evidence of full reimbursements to affected beneficiaries (or authorized designees) to meet the burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements for a designee (reimbursement recipient)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraph (h)(5)(xi) and similar provisions, a designee must be an individual or entity for whom the beneficiary has provided the petitioner or its successor in interest prior written authorization to receive such reimbursement, as long as the petitioner or its successor in interest, or its agent, employer, or any joint employer, attorney, facilitator, recruiter, or similar employment service would not act as such designee or derive any financial benefit, either directly or indirectly, from the reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain clear prior written authorization from the beneficiary if reimbursements will be paid to a designee; the designee must be independent and not financially tied to the petitioner or its agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year denial period for subsequent petitions after prohibited-fee denial/revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will deny any H-2A or H-2B petition filed by the same petitioner or a successor in interest within 1 year after the decision denying or revoking on notice an H-2B or H-2A petition on the basis of prohibited fee collection (provided the denied/revoked petition was filed on or after January 17, 2025). USCIS will also deny petitions within 1 year after withdrawal of an H-2A or H-2B petition filed on or after January 17, 2025 that was withdrawn following USCIS issuance of an RFE or notice of intent to deny/revoke on the same basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that a denial/revocation for prohibited fees creates a 1-year bar on filing subsequent H-2 petitions by the same petitioner/successor absent relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional 3-year denial period and reimbursement as condition for future approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: For an additional 3 years after the 1-year period, USCIS will deny any H-2A or H-2B petition filed by the same petitioner or successor in interest, unless the petitioner or successor demonstrates to USCIS that the petitioner/successor or its agent/facilitator/recruiter or any joint employer reimbursed in full each beneficiary, or the beneficiary's designee only if such beneficiary cannot be located or is deceased, of the denied or revoked petition from whom a prohibited fee was collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full reimbursement of affected beneficiaries (or authorized designees) can be a condition to end the extended denial period; collect and present proof of reimbursements if seeking to overcome this bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor in interest — factors for determining successor status
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the 1-year and 3-year denial provisions, successor in interest means an employer that is controlling and carrying on the business of a previous employer regardless of whether such successor has succeeded to all rights and liabilities. Factors considered (no one factor dispositive): (i) substantial continuity of same business operations; (ii) use of same facilities; (iii) substantial continuity of the workforce; (iv) similarity of jobs and working conditions; (v) similarity of supervisory personnel; (vi) whether former management/owner retains direct or indirect interest; (vii) similarity in machinery, equipment, production methods, or assets required; (viii) similarity of products and services; (ix) familial/close personal relationships between predecessor and successor owners; (x) use of same or related remittance sources for business payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare documentation addressing these factors if successor status is relevant to adjudication or denial consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B petitioner agreements and notification requirements (parallel to H-2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must notify DHS, within 2 workdays, if: an H-2B worker does not report for work within 5 workdays after employment start date; the nonagricultural labor/services were completed more than 30 days early; or an H-2B worker does not report for work for 5 consecutive workdays without consent or is terminated prior to completion. The petitioner must retain evidence of such notification for a 1-year period. In filing an H-2B petition, the petitioner and each employer consent to allow Government access to sites and to cooperate with compliance reviews; failure to cooperate may result in denial or revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the same notification timelines and record-retention practices as for H-2A; ensure cooperation with USCIS inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of temporary services or labor and petitioner's need categories (H-2B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary services or labor under H-2B refers to any job in which the petitioner's need for the duties to be performed is temporary. Employment is of a temporary nature when the employer needs a worker for a limited period of time — generally limited to one year or less, but in the case of a one-time event could last up to 3 years. The petitioner's need shall be a one-time occurrence, a seasonal need, a peak load need, or an intermittent need. Specific evidentiary criteria: (1) One-time occurrence — petitioner must establish it has not employed workers in the past for these services and will not need them in the future, or that a temporary short event created the need; (2) Seasonal need — petitioner must establish services are traditionally tied to a season and recurring, and specify periods each year when services are not needed; (3) Peakload need — petitioner must establish it regularly employs permanent workers and needs to supplement staff temporarily due to short-term demand and that temporary additions will not become regular; (4) Intermittent need — petitioner must establish it has not employed permanent/full-time workers to perform the services but occasionally needs temporary workers for short periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation tailored to the claimed category of need (historical employment records, seasonal schedules, evidence of peak demand, and explanations demonstrating temporariness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures — prior temporary labor certification application requirement for H-2B petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing a petition with the director to classify an alien as an H-2B worker, the petitioner shall apply for a temporary labor certification with the Secretary of Labor for all areas of the United States, except the Territory of Guam. In Guam, the petitioning employer shall apply for a temporary labor certification with the Governor of Guam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file the USCIS petition to classify an alien as H-2B until the required DOL (or Guam governor) temporary labor certification application has been filed as specified.
